name: Milano-Torino
description: Campari and sweet vermouth over ice with an orange slice. The Americano before the soda.
history: Served by Gaspare Campari at his Caffè Camparino in Milan in the mid-19th century. The name pairs Campari from Milan with vermouth from Turin. Add soda and it becomes the Americano; add gin and it becomes the Negroni.
whyItWorks: Equal parts bitter and sweet, so neither wins. It is the base of the whole Negroni family.
steps: Build Campari and sweet vermouth over ice in a rocks glass.
Stir briefly and add an orange slice.
techniqueNotes: Fresh vermouth matters more here than in a Negroni; there is nothing else to hide behind.
creator: Gaspare Campari
